title: ‘Money Monster’ Taps into Anger of Every Man vs Wall Street

image.attribution: RIA Novosti archive, image #978776 / Alexey Kudenko / CC-BY-SA-3.0

main_content:
Money Monster, a film directed by Jodie Foster and starring George Clooney and Julia Roberts, is the latest installment in a movie genre trying to tackle the huge gap between the uber-rich 1 percent and everyone else.

At times emotional, at times schmaltzy, it is still perhaps the most promising star-studded production to try and reach the masses with a story about the corrupting power of money.

The film centers on Lee Gates, played by Clooney. Gates is the sleek and fast-talking anchor of a popular financial TV show called Money Monster. Gates is a man at the top of his game.

Investors follow his tips, and his hold on the stock market is golden — until that fateful day when the market tumbles and people like delivery man Kyle Budwell lose everything.

“I think this film is an interesting combination of being able to be an accessible mainstream ‘popcorn movie,’ but it forces you to learn at the same time about something that is quite complicated,” Foster said.

Clooney offers a good performance as the cocky TV anchor who realizes that he, too, is a victim — conned into relaying false information that played a huge part in destroying people’s lives. From that point onward, he is determined to get to the truth.

Clooney feels it is a movie for the masses. “When all these things go wrong, the little guy gets screwed,” he said.

Despite some structural weaknesses, Money Monster has merit as one of the first films about the Wall Street collapse to tell the tale of a regular guy who lost everything. A guy who, along with plenty of people in the audience, is struggling with the fear, anger, and bad memories of the 2008 financial collapse.

questions.question: What is Money Monster’s theme?
options: The journey of a financial expert to regain his credibility.
The struggle between the richest 1 percent and the average person.
An exploration of the life of a delivery man turned billionaire.
The moral dilemmas faced by wealthy investors during financial crises.
questions.answer: The struggle between the richest 1 percent and the average person.

questions.question: What character is George Clooney playing in the movie?
options: A delivery man who loses everything.
A determined journalist uncovering financial fraud.
A wealthy investor making risky trades.
Lee Gates, a fast-talking TV financial anchor.
questions.answer: Lee Gates, a fast-talking TV financial anchor.

questions.question: How does the director describe her own movie?
options: As a dramatic portrayal of financial success.
As a pop culture phenomenon that ignores serious topics.
As an accessible mainstream movie that educates about complicated issues.
As an underwhelming attempt to critique the financial system.
questions.answer: As an accessible mainstream movie that educates about complicated issues.
